title: A Alibi for the Confession
premise: Estate lawyer Felix Sandoval has spent fifteen years as the quiet keeper of Marlow Bend's secrets, until a will surfaces bearing the signature of a man who died two decades ago—and a body dressed in clothes stolen from her own closet turns up in the courthouse basement. As she decodes a ledger hidden in the firm's filing system, Felix realizes the dead man faked his death to expose a cover-up that implicates the judge who raised her. The killer is the town's beloved sheriff, who has been silencing witnesses one by one; in the end, Felix chooses justice over loyalty, broadcasting the decoded ledger at the founder's day ceremony and surrendering her own fabricated identity to the truth.
about_author: Mara Crane is the pen name of a former small-town paralegal who spent a decade watching secrets move through probate files and swore some of them deserved daylight. She writes mysteries about ordinary people whose tidy lives come undone by paper trails.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Felix Sandoval opens a probate file containing a will signed by Edmund Voss—dead for twenty years. Her hands shake; she's the only one who'd recognize the forgery because she helped bury the original estate. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Felix searches the firm's archives and finds Voss's original death certificate with an impossible second signature: Judge Harlan Crane, the man who took her in as a runaway teen. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the first crack in fifteen years of carefully filed loyalty.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: A stranger is found dead in the courthouse basement wearing Felix's own missing gray blazer and scarf. Sheriff Dale Pruitt treats her as witness, not suspect—but his questions feel like traps. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: invisibility failing, panic beneath composure.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Local journalist Nia Okafor reveals she saw someone leaving the basement wearing 'a lawyer's clothes'—and that she's been investigating Voss's death for months. She wants Felix's records. POV: Nia. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two women who keep secrets differently.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Filing
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how teenage Felix arrived in Marlow Bend with no name worth keeping, and how Judge Crane gave her a new identity and a job in exchange for silence about what she saw the night Voss 'died.' POV: Felix (past). Emotional beat: gratitude tangled with debt.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Felix discovers the firm's client index numbers correspond to dates and payments—a coded ledger of hush money running through twenty years of estates. The final entry is dated next week. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the thrill of decoding curdling into fear of what it means.

chapters.title: Sheriff's Questions
chapters.summary: Pruitt interviews Felix again, revealing he knows about her missing clothes before she reports them stolen. He mentions Voss by name though the case was never public. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: realizing the hunter knows she's hunting.

chapters.title: Nia's Box of Clippings
chapters.summary: Nia shows Felix twenty years of suppressed stories: a drowned girl, a burned diner, three 'accidents' all connected to men named in the ledger. Someone at the newspaper killed each story. POV: Nia. Emotional beat: righteous anger meeting Felix's caution.

chapters.title: The Judge's Dinner
chapters.summary: Judge Crane hosts his annual dinner and warns Felix, gently, to stop pulling threads—for her own good. He calls her 'the daughter I chose,' and she can't tell if it's love or leverage. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: love against duty, the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Second Body, Same Closet
chapters.summary: The county clerk is found dead, also dressed in clothes from Felix's closet. The frame is tightening; Pruitt announces he's seeking a warrant. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: from suspect to prey—the trap closing on schedule.

chapters.title: Running the Numbers
chapters.summary: Felix and Nia work through the ledger overnight and identify the paymaster: not Crane, but a shell company tied to Pruitt's family land holdings. Every silenced witness threatened the sheriff's empire. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: revelation's cold clarity.

chapters.title: Edmund Voss, Alive
chapters.summary: A letter arrives postmarked the day the body was found: Voss confesses he faked his death, hid in plain sight, and built the will as a time capsule meant to be opened only if he was killed. He names his killer as 'the law itself.' POV: Felix reading. Emotional beat: grief for a ghost who trusted her.

chapters.title: The Safe Deposit Key
chapters.summary: Following the will's odd bequest clause, Felix finds a safe deposit box containing Voss's full evidence—including photos implicating Crane in the original cover-up, not as murderer but as protector-turned-accomplice. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the floor giving out beneath her oldest loyalty.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Courthouse Steps
chapters.summary: Felix confronts Crane. He admits everything: he buried Voss's real death report to protect the town's economy, then protected Felix because she saw too much. He begs her to let it stay buried. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: love and duty finally at open war.

chapters.title: The Warrant
chapters.summary: Pruitt arrests Felix for the murders, presenting planted evidence—her fingerprints, her clothes, a forged motive. In holding, she realizes only the ledger, publicly decoded, can save her. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: despair sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Nia's Deadline
chapters.summary: Nia races to verify the ledger independently while Pruitt moves to have Felix transferred out of county—to a jurisdiction where the evidence will vanish. POV: Nia. Emotional beat: a journalist's race against institutional erasure.

chapters.title: The Cell Confession
chapters.summary: Crane visits Felix in jail and offers to confess to the old cover-up if she'll let him take the fall for the murders too—an alibi built from a false confession. She refuses: she won't build her freedom on another lie. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: refusing the easy injustice, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Founder's Day
chapters.summary: Released pending trial on Crane's bond, Felix walks into the Founder's Day ceremony where Pruitt is being honored—and where Voss's will, per its terms, must be publicly read aloud. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: terror and purpose braided together.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: As the will is read, Felix interjects, decoding the ledger aloud before the whole town, matching names to dates to deaths. Nia live-streams it. The crowd's murmur becomes a roar as Pruitt's name lands last. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken where lies were crowned.

chapters.title: Sheriff's Fall
chapters.summary: Pruitt draws his weapon, but deputies who grew up on his payroll hear their fathers' names in the ledger and lower theirs instead. He's taken into state custody as federal agents arrive—Voss had mailed copies everywhere. POV: multiple. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, outside the law's own house.

chapters.title: What the Record Shows
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Crane pleads to obstruction and resigns; Voss's true death is ruled murder, closed. Felix testifies under her real, long-buried birth name, choosing truth over the identity Crane built for her. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: mourning the father-figure while reclaiming the self.

chapters.title: A Clean File
chapters.summary: Felix reopens her practice with a new rule: no secret-keeping clients. Nia publishes the full story; a package arrives containing Voss's last letter, thanking her for opening the time capsule. She files it under her own name. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—invisibility traded for integrity.
